In the time before time, when the sky was empty and black, there lived a lonely weaver named Celeste who dwelt at the edge of the world. She possessed a loom of silver threads, but had nothing beautiful to create.

One night, she wept tears of sorrow into her loom. Each tear transformed into a glowing droplet of light. Amazed, Celeste began to weave these luminous tears into patterns across her loom, creating spirals, clusters, and rivers of brilliance.

As she worked through the eternal darkness, her creations grew too large for her loom. She cast them upward, and they stuck to the vast canvas of night. These became the first stars.

The Sun, who had been sleeping beneath the world, awoke to see the beauty Celeste had made. Moved by her artistry, he offered her a choice: join him in the sky and shine forever, or remain on earth as a mortal.

Celeste chose to stay, saying, "My purpose is to create beauty for others, not to become it."

To honor her sacrifice, the Sun decreed that her star-patterns would guide travelers forever, and that humans would always look up in wonder, remembering the weaver who transformed loneliness into light.

Each night, as mortals closed their eyes, Arachne would descend from her cosmic web and gather the day's forgotten thoughts—the fleeting wishes, the half-remembered songs, the shadows of hope and fear. With eight nimble legs, she would weave these fragments into intricate patterns that became the dreams of sleeping souls.

But Arachne grew lonely in her work. She longed to create something permanent, something that would last beyond the morning's light. So one night, she wove herself into her own creation, becoming part of the dream-web itself.

Now, when you dream of falling through endless space, you are sliding down one of Arachne's silver threads. When you dream of flying, you are dancing across her web. And when you wake with the fading memory of something beautiful you cannot quite recall, that is Arachne's gentle reminder that she is still weaving, still creating, still connecting all dreamers across the infinite night.
